paragraphs: Friend, Paul is full of big plans: Spain, Rome, Jerusalem. But look at who gets the credit, because he will not presume to speak of anything except "what Christ has accomplished through me" (Romans 15:18). He says it was the grace God gave him that made him a minister to the Gentiles (Romans 15:15-16). The best workers I know say, "I just showed up, and HE did the rest."

Now look at how Paul treats the believers in Rome. He's convinced they are "full of goodness, brimming with knowledge, and able to instruct one another" (Romans 15:14), and he still writes them a bold reminder. Nobody is too wise to be reminded, and nobody is too small to be trusted with the truth. Even an apostle asks them to "join me in my struggle by praying to God for me" (Romans 15:30), so I'm not too proud to ask either.

Paul's plans are held loosely, friend. He hopes to see Rome so that "by God’s will" he may come with joy (Romans 15:32), and he stops first to carry a gift to the poor saints in Jerusalem (Romans 15:25-27). So here's the takeaway, baker: work hard, give gladly, pray for each other, and let God hold the calendar. Then you can end the day like Paul: "The God of peace be with all of you. Amen." (Romans 15:33)
